feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Trump says developing AI is a critical race, downplaying fears
entry.summary: President Trump continues to support frontier artificial intelligence development, despite industry fears such technology could destroy humanity, casting AI as a critical race against China.

entry.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders says Congress has gotten a 'wake-up call' on AI risks
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders,I-Vermont, about his concerns over the risks of artificial intelligence.

entry.title: Trump says Ukraine and Russia agreed to stop attacks on energy sites
entry.summary: In the face of soaring diesel prices, President Trump claims Ukraine and Russia have agreed to halt strikes on each other's energy sites.

entry.title: For thousands of Haitians in the U.S., end of protected status brings fear, grief and defiance
entry.summary: Haitians in the U.S. lost their Temporary Protected Status under Trump's immigration crackdown. Now facing deportation to a homeland wracked by gang violence, disease and extreme poverty, Haitians in Miami are meeting the moment with grief, anger, and courage.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: President Trump downplays fears about AI risks, Supreme Court rejects Trump's efforts to enact mail-in voting restrictions for the midterms, Kennedy Center says it's on the brink of bankruptcy.

entry.title: Anthropic co-founder says slowing AI is a 'collective action problem'
entry.summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark discusses growing concerns about artificial intelligence, recent warning signs and what he says companies should do to reduce the risks.

entry.title: What the 10-year Treasury yield hitting 5% means for inflation and the Fed
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Stacey Vanek Smith, reporter for Bloomberg Businessweek, about the 10-year Treasury yield's brief rise to 5% Monday and how the Federal Reserve might react.

entry.title: In Florida, textbook publishers are minimizing or removing climate change coverage
entry.summary: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.

entry.title: Designer Bob Mackie dies at 87
entry.summary: Bob Mackie, designer of glitzy costumes for stage and screen, died Monday of pneumonia in Palm Springs, California.

entry.title: Supreme Court refuses to allow Trump's mail voting restrictions for the midterms
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected President Trump's push for new mail-in voting restrictions for the midterm election.
